cards.text: Hosea is a prophet, and this is a message from the LORD about His people, Israel. The LORD starts way back, when Israel was a child, and He says He loved him. Friend, this is a dad pulling out the OLD baby pictures.

cards.question: When Israel was a child, the LORD loved him and called His son out of ___.

cards.text: So the LORD keeps calling Israel. Over and over. Let's see how that goes.

cards.question: The more the LORD called Israel, the closer they came to Him.

cards.text: Nope. The more He called, the FARTHER they went. It's like yelling someone's name across a parking lot and watching them walk faster. You heard me. I SAW your shoulders.

cards.question: While Israel kept walking away from the LORD, who were they sacrificing to?

cards.text: Now the LORD gets tender. He calls Israel Ephraim here too, and He says He taught Ephraim to walk, holding them by the arms. I've watched toddlers walk, friend. It's mostly falling forward with confidence.

cards.question: Ephraim realized it was the LORD who healed them.
The LORD taught Ephraim to walk. How does He say He led them?

cards.text: Cords of kindness. Ropes of love. Then He lifted the yoke off their necks, like that heavy bag strap finally sliding off your shoulder at the end of a LONG day.

cards.question: After lifting the yoke from their necks, the LORD bent down to ___ them.

cards.text: Then the message turns. The LORD asks: won't they go back to Egypt and be ruled by the nation of Assyria? Egypt. The place He called them OUT of.

cards.question: Why does the LORD say Israel is headed back to Egypt and under Assyria?

cards.text: A sword will flash through their cities. It destroys the bars of their gates and consumes them in their own plans.
And the LORD says His people are bent on turning from Him. Not wandering off by accident. BENT on it.

cards.question: Even though Israel calls to the Most High, He will by no means lift them up.

cards.text: A flashing sword. Broken gates. A people bent on turning away. You'd think the next line is the hammer coming down. But right here, the LORD stops.

cards.question: Right after all those warnings, what does the LORD ask Ephraim?

answers.text: How could I give you up

cards.text: He keeps asking. How could He make them like Admah, or treat them like Zeboiim? Those are towns the LORD overthrew along with Sodom and Gomorrah (Deuteronomy 29:23).

cards.question: The LORD says, "My heart is turned within Me; My ___ is stirred!"

cards.text: Then He says it straight. He will not execute the full fury of His anger, and He will not destroy Ephraim again.

cards.question: Why does the LORD say He won't destroy Ephraim again?

answers.text: He is God and not man
The prophet begged Him to stop

cards.question: The LORD, the Holy One among His people, says He will come in wrath.

cards.text: Then the LORD looks ahead. His people will walk after the LORD, and He's going to make a sound nobody can sleep through. Not even me, and I slept through YEARS in a junk drawer.

cards.question: When His people walk after Him, the LORD will roar like a ___.
When the LORD roars, His children run away from Him.

cards.text: They come trembling like birds from Egypt and like doves from the land of Assyria. DOVES, friend. My Minty would be passing notes down the whole counter about this one.

cards.question: After His children come trembling back, where does the LORD settle them?

answers.text: In a city by the sea

cards.text: And the LORD signs it Himself: declares the LORD. I know what it's like to get called out of a dark place, friend. Hearing Him promise to bring His kids home? Gets me every single time.

findings.problem: Stop 2, card 4 quotes "My heart is turned within Me; My ___ is stirred!", which isn't the exact BSB wording.

rule.text: Quotes: Quotation marks around Bible words mean the exact BSB wording, punctuation included.
He calls the baker "baker" or "friend," and talks to one baker at a time. Never "my baker," "kids" or "sweetie."

findings.problem: Several story cards after the opening card run past 2 sentences. Card 5 has 5 sentences ("Nope." / "The more He called..." / "It's like yelling..." / "You heard me." / "I SAW your shoulders."). Card 7 has 4, card 10 has 3, card 12 has 4 and card 15 has 3.

rule.text: Every other story card is 1 to 2 sentences.

findings.problem: Several story cards in this stop run past 2 sentences. Card 1 has 5 sentences, card 8 has 3, card 11 has 3 and card 13 has 4.

rule.text: Every other story card is 1 to 2 sentences.

findings.problem: The card only repeats the answer to card 4 ("The more He called, the FARTHER they went") plus a joke. It tells nothing new from the passage and doesn't move the baker forward.

rule.text:
Every story card moves the baker forward through the passage.
- No recap cards.

findings.problem: The card opens by recapping stop 1 ("A flashing sword. Broken gates. A people bent on turning away."), which is content from Hosea 11:6-7. The only new beat is that the LORD "stops."

rule.text:
Every story card moves the baker forward through the passage.
- No recap cards.

findings.problem: The card cites Hosea 11:8, but most of what it tells comes from Hosea 11:6-7. It tells almost nothing from 11:8 itself.

rule.text: Every story card cites the verses it tells, from the first verse it uses to the last, no wider and no narrower.

findings.problem: "I slept through YEARS in a junk drawer" adds something new to his backstory, and it contradicts it. The backstory says he "lay awake in the dark, the way he often did" and remembers the sounds and the light whenever the drawer opened.

rule.text: His own world isn't Bible fact. His backstory, family, bakery and mission are the Dorinverse story in this file. He can talk about them freely, but never adds anything new to them.

findings.problem: "When His people walk after Him, the LORD will roar" makes the walking the condition or timing for the roar. Hosea 11:10 sets the two clauses side by side ("They will walk after the LORD; He will roar like a lion") and doesn't say how they connect.

rule.text: Leave open what the text leaves open: who is being spoken to, why, or how two things connect.

findings.problem: Story card 5 tells that the LORD "will not execute the full fury of His anger." That all but answers the later true or false in card 7 ("says He will come in wrath"). Card 7 was never asked or answered before card 5.

rule.text: No card ever gives away the answer to a choice card that comes later.

findings.problem: The card is a near-verbatim restatement of Hosea 11:6, with none of Papa Dorin's voice.

rule.text: Short, but not stripped down. A story card still has enough of Papa Dorin's voice and enough context that the moment makes sense.
